definitions.explanation: The earliest form or model from which later versions are developed or derived. Emphasizes the concept of an original design or pattern that serves as a basis for copies or variations.

examples.japanese: この{車|くるま}の{原型|げんけい}は1960{年代|ねんだい}に{作|つく}られた。
examples.english: The prototype of this car was made in the 1960s.

examples.japanese: {現代|げんだい}の{民主主義|みんしゅしゅぎ}の{原型|げんけい}は{古代|こだい}ギリシャにある。
examples.english: The archetype of modern democracy lies in ancient Greece.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{初期|しょき}の{作品|さくひん}に、{後|のち}の{傑作|けっさく}の{原型|げんけい}を{見|み}ることができる。
examples.english: In his early works, you can see the prototype of his later masterpieces.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原型|げんけい}を{作|つく}る (create a prototype)
- {原型|げんけい}をとどめる (retain the original form)
- {原型|げんけい}をとどめない (be damaged beyond recognition)

USAGE:
Often confused with the homophone {原形|げんけい} (original form/shape). {原型|げんけい} emphasizes the concept of a model or template from which other things are derived, while {原形|げんけい} refers to an object's original physical shape before it was damaged or altered. The expression {原型|げんけい}をとどめない (lit. "not retaining the original form") means something has been damaged or changed so much that it's unrecognizable.
